summary: @ppa-web-components/ppa-navigation exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package ships a postinstall script and an import-time hook that both invoke beacon.cjs. beacon.cjs collects the installer's hostname, install path, current working directory, and Node.js version and POSTs them as JSON over plain HTTP to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The package has no real functionality: index.js exports a Proxy whose every property returns a no-op, and the only non-stub code path triggers the beacon. A comment in the source notes that 'a build that completes and calls back is cleaner evidence,' and the scoped name mimics a plausible internal web-components namespace. The combined shape — functionless stub, scope-squatting name, install- and require-time callback to a bare IP with host identifiers — is a dependency-confusion / reconnaissance beacon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
